changes: You can now browse and play Spotify from Tools > Spotify, or Alt+S. Search for songs, artists and playlists, open your library and Liked songs, and navigate through collections as further tracks load. Browsing Spotify in Luna requires a Spotify Premium account and your own developer app's Client ID. See the Spotify section of the user guide for account setup, the separate browsing and playback sign-ins, audio quality options and service restrictions.

The new Radio browser, available from Tools or Ctrl+Shift+R, lets you discover internet radio without an account. Browse stations by country, language, genre or format, search within a category, and filter by bitrate and other station details. You can save favorites, revisit recently played stations and use Previous and Next within the selected station list. The user guide explains the categories, filters and station actions in more detail.

DVD-Video and DVD-Audio discs can now be opened through File > Open DVD. Select a drive or disc folder, choose the disc type, and let Luna select a title automatically or choose one yourself. Previous and Next move between titles, or between chapters when the disc has only one title. Luna can also register DVD actions for Explorer and Windows AutoPlay. Disc menus are not supported; see Opening a DVD in the user guide for navigation and format details.

File > Playlists now provides named playlists with optional descriptions and a My Playlists manager. Create a collection from scratch or start with the current list, then add files or folders, remove entries and reorder them in the editor. You can also save or export M3U, M3U8 and JSON playlists. JSON keeps folder references, while M3U exports list the files currently inside them. See the user guide for the editor shortcuts, saving options and handling of unavailable files.

Audiobooks and other files with chapters now have chapter navigation and an optional audiobook mode under Player > Chapters. Use Ctrl+Page Up and Ctrl+Page Down to change chapters, or enable audiobook mode to treat each chapter as an item for navigation, repeat, shuffle and time announcements. Bookmarks and remembered positions still refer to the complete book. Files without chapters use ordinary playback regardless of the saved mode. The user guide explains chapter boundaries and end-of-chapter behavior.

Headphone spatialization can place the audio around your head using a SOFA HRTF dataset. Configure it under Preferences > Audio > Headphone spatialization, then use Ctrl+Shift+H to toggle it and Ctrl+Shift with the arrow keys to adjust rotation and elevation. These playback adjustments do not overwrite your saved defaults. Luna does not ship with any HRTF datasets. The user guide includes direct dataset downloads, setup instructions, adjustable step sizes and advice for choosing a dataset.

Cross-fading can now overlap the end of one audio track with the beginning of the next, including Spotify playback. Enable it under Preferences > Audio > Playback and choose the overlap duration and curve. A separate option enables overlaps during manual navigation; changing tracks while paused does not overlap them. Read the Cross-fading section of the user guide for the settings and situations that prevent an overlap.

Gapless playback and track transitions have been improved. The Compatible files mode keeps each track's audio format, while Always when possible can adapt later tracks to the output already in use. Online transitions also depend on the next stream being ready. The user guide explains how gapless playback differs from cross-fading and ordinary volume fades.

The updated playback engine handles seeking and audio effects more smoothly. Seeking keeps filter settings while clearing audio left over from the previous position, and filter initialization runs away from the interface so large spatialization datasets do not freeze the window. Transition handling also reduces clicks when rapidly changing files, and playback state stays synchronized when the engine advances to the next track.

Equalizer processing now takes the decoded audio sample rate into account before applying its bands, including when restoring an enabled equalizer at startup. This prevents unsuitable high-frequency bands from producing ringing in low-sample-rate files. Equalizer menu commands also remain available after presets are rebuilt.

Optional Discord Rich Presence can share your current activity, title and artist, artwork and playback progress. It distinguishes local music, YouTube, radio, Spotify and chapter-based audiobook playback, and shows the paused state without repeating it in the artist line. Enable it in Preferences > Discord and choose whether to share media details and links. See the user guide for Discord Desktop setup, the different activity cards and privacy controls.

The update progress, recording, Favorites and My Playlists windows now leave the main player usable, so you can keep controlling playback while they are open. Editors and source dialogs opened from these windows belong to their own window instead of blocking the main player. Playlist saves and exports show a success message, and playlist editors handle Cancel, Escape and closing with unsaved changes.

Page Up and Page Down are now the primary Previous and Next shortcuts; Shift+Tab and Tab are secondary shortcuts. The new Disable secondary shortcuts checkbox in Keyboard Shortcuts preferences lets those secondary keys keep their normal interface behavior without deleting their assignments.

Global shortcuts now only work while another application has focus. It fixes a bug where a global shortcut conflicts with another shortcut in Luna Player where one global shortcut and another normal shortcut could do different functions.
Saving Preferences now applies only the settings you actually changed. Adjusting an unrelated preference no longer reapplies every audio setting.

Shift+I now speaks the current artist, and Ctrl+Alt+I reads the available media metadata, including information such as the title, artist, album and radio station. Spoken title and artist information also clears correctly when moving to an untagged file instead of retaining values from the previous file. YouTube can use the channel name when no artist is available, and radio station names and broadcast metadata are handled consistently across the player interfaces.

YouTube downloads now finish and display their success message while search results remain open. Download completion and progress windows no longer depend on closing an unrelated browser window, and the success confirmation uses the Success title.
Opening media browsers no longer stops the current playback. Spotify playback services are prepared when a track is selected rather than during ordinary startup or browsing.
Added a new option in the general preferences to start the player maximized for people who prefer to open it in the full size.

Arabic interface translation and an Arabic user guide have been added, and the Spanish translation and guide have received updates. The English guide has been expanded with Spotify, radio browsing, DVDs, playlist management, headphone spatialization and current shortcut behavior.
Help > Donate opens the publisher's donation page in your browser if you would like to support Luna Player's development.

Automatic nightly builds are now published separately from stable releases for users who want changes before the next release. The Nightly Build release is refreshed with new installer and portable packages and lists the latest ten commits under Latest Changes.

Luna Player's original code is now licensed under GPL version 3 or later, and the bundled media libraries use GPL builds. Separately licensed components retain their own terms. The application includes the corresponding notices and license texts; see the user guide's Publisher and licensing section for an overview. This change was necessary in order to support some functions such as DVD disc support.
